limitations.statement: Every headline result (55.2% relative error reduction, 29.1 BLEU, 2.5/2.7 WER, dataset-scaling curve) is a single-run point estimate; no seeds, repeats, or variance are reported anywhere in the evidence, so statistical reliability of comparisons cannot be assessed.
limitations.effect_on_interpretation: Comparative and magnitude claims are reported as point estimates only; none can be described as statistically significant.

limitations.statement: Several robustness results (noise robustness, long-form comparison, negative-transfer curve, human-comparison figure) are read from figures rather than tabulated numbers, and are marked extracted_from_image/soft.
limitations.effect_on_interpretation: These trends are reported qualitatively (direction and approximate crossover conditions) rather than with exact per-point numbers.

limitations.statement: Baselines for multilingual recognition, translation, and language ID are quoted from prior publications rather than re-run under Whisper's exact evaluation and text-normalization conditions.
limitations.effect_on_interpretation: Cross-system comparisons are indicative, not controlled; the authors themselves flag this as limiting direct comparability.

limitations.statement: Only zero-shot transfer was evaluated; fine-tuning on target datasets was not studied, and the dataset-size ablation shows only ~1 WER point of further gain from 54,000 to 680,000 hours, so the value of the very largest scale is not established for every task.
limitations.effect_on_interpretation: The central scaling claim is best read as 'scale up to roughly 50-80k hours is clearly beneficial'; benefits of scaling to the full 680k hours are smaller and task-dependent, and fine-tuned performance is unknown.
